newsitem.title: TURKEY: SOCCER-BOKSIC'S GOAL TAKES JUVENTUS TO VICTORY OVER FENERBAHCE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BOKSIC'S GOAL TAKES JUVENTUS TO VICTORY OVER FENERBAHCE.

text.p: A solitary goal from Alen Boksic in the 21st minute gave reigning European champions Juventus victory over Fenerbahce of Turkey on Wednesday in the first Champions' League match ever played in Asia.

Juventus, playing in the Fenerbahce stadium on Istanbul's Asian shore, showed themselves to be impervious to the din created by thousands of Turkish fans pounding drums and screaming from the first to the final whistle.
Boksic's goal came when the nervous Fenerbahce side lost possession in the penalty area, allowing the Croatian striker to swoop and fire into the back of the net.
The Istanbul team had the first goal attempt when a header by Bosnian forward Elvir Bolic in the 10th minute off an angled pass from Tarik Dasgun skimmed over the bar.
Bolic had another chance in the 30th minute but collided with Juventus goalkeeper Michelangelo Rampulla just in front of the goal and shot wide.
Both Turks and Italians squandered several chances to score in the second half but a relaxed Juventus, taking their second victory in two Group C games, managed to keep the upper hand.

Juventus could have increased their lead twice just after the break when French midfielder Zinedine Zidane shot wide in the 51st minute and Turkey's international keeper Rustu Recber stopped a Christian Vieri header in the 56th.
Juventus coach Marcello Lippi said Fenerbahce had made his team fight to the very end.
"Although we managed to keep control for the hour after Boksic's goal, they created several very dangerous chances towards the end," Lippi said. "The match was fast paced."
Substitute Erol Bulut just missed scoring the equaliser in the 84th minute when his close-range header was intercepted by Rampulla, who was standing in for the injured Angelo Peruzzi.
Fenerbahce's Brazilian coach Sebastiao Lazaroni said he was happy with his team's performance.
"Juventus made good use of their one chance in the first half but we played well in the second. We could have scored around three goals," he said. "All the players put up a good fight."

Fenerbahce: 1-Rustu Recber, 2-Ilker Yagcioglu, 3-Uche Okechukwu, 4-Jes Hogh, 5-Kemalettin Senturk, 6-Halil Ibrahim Kaya, 8-Tuncay Akgun (15-Erol Bulut 83rd), 9-Elvir Bolic, 10-Jay Jay Okacha, 16-Bulent Uygun, 19-Tarik Dasgun (25-Benhur Babaoglu 88th).

Juventus - 12-Michelangelo Rampulla, 2-Ciro Ferrara, 4-Paolo Montero, 4-Sergio Porrini, 8-Antonio Conte, 9, Alen Boksic, 10-Alessandro Del Piero (20-Alessio Tacchinardi 85th), 14-Didier Deschamps, 15-Christian Vieri (11-Michele Padovano 59th minute), 21-Zinedine Zidane (7-Angelo Di Livio 71st), 22-Gianluca Pesetto.
